name: When the World Came to Town: Great Exhibitions
description: Crystal halls, iron towers and space-age pavilions: the fairs where nations showed off their machines and the public first saw the future.

checkpoints.name: Iron and glass
checkpoints.note: Prince Albert's idea becomes the Great Exhibition of 1851, housed in Joseph Paxton's Crystal Palace and opened by Queen Victoria. Paris answers with the Exposition Universelle of 1855, and the fair becomes a way to show national pride.

checkpoints.name: Towers and wheels
checkpoints.note: The Centennial Exposition shows Alexander Graham Bell's telephone. In Paris the Eiffel Tower, built by Gustave Eiffel, rises for the 1889 fair, and Chicago's Columbian Exposition shows off the first Ferris wheel and an early zipper. The 1900 Paris fair marks the height of the Belle Epoque.

checkpoints.name: The fair as future
checkpoints.note: Even in the Depression, fairs in Chicago, Paris and New York kept going, and the 1939 New York World's Fair builds a picture of tomorrow just as war begins. The big fairs pause through the war years, and when they return they look to the postwar world.

checkpoints.name: Space-age pavilions
checkpoints.note: Brussels shows the Atomium in 1958, Seattle raises the Space Needle for the Century 21 Exposition, and New York's 1964 fair features Walt Disney's attractions. Expo 67 in Montreal and Expo 70 in Osaka bring huge crowds.

checkpoints.name: The modern expo
checkpoints.note: Expo 86 in Vancouver and Expo 2010 in Shanghai show the fair still draws visitors in the age of television and the internet, as host cities use them to show a new face to the world.
